topic: Mechanics I: Kinematics and Newton's Laws of Motion
description: Mechanics is the foundational branch of classical physics dealing with the motion of bodies and the forces that act upon them. Kinematics describes the motion, while Newton's Laws of Motion (NLM) explain the causes of motion, forming a critical pillar for competitive exams like NEET and JEE.

sections.title: Kinematics: Fundamentals and Motion in 1D
sections.description: The study of motion of an object along a straight line without considering the forces causing the motion.

key_concepts.explanation: Distance is the actual path length traveled (scalar), while displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between initial and final positions (vector).
Speed is the rate of distance covered (scalar), whereas velocity is the rate of change of displacement (vector).
The rate of change of velocity with respect to time. It can be uniform (constant) or non-uniform (variable).

scientific_principles.application: Used to find unknown kinematic parameters of an object moving in a straight line with constant acceleration.

sections.title: Motion in a Plane (2D Kinematics)
sections.description: The study of motion in two dimensions, including the use of vectors to analyze displacement, velocity, and acceleration.

key_concepts.explanation: Physical quantities possessing both magnitude and direction, which follow the triangle or parallelogram laws of vector addition.
A form of motion where a particle is thrown obliquely near the earth's surface, moving along a curved (parabolic) path under the action of gravity alone.
Motion of an object along a circular path with a constant speed, characterized by constant change in direction and centripetal acceleration.

important_facts.fact: In projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity remains constant throughout the flight because there is no acceleration in the horizontal direction (ignoring air resistance).
Maximum horizontal range for a projectile is achieved when the angle of projection is exactly 45 degrees.

sections.title: Newton's Laws of Motion (NLM)
sections.description: The fundamental principles governing classical mechanics, describing the relationship between a body and the forces acting upon it.

historical_events.significance: Isaac Newton published his three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, laying the absolute groundwork for classical mechanics.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by an external unbalanced force.
scientific_principles.application: Explains everyday phenomena like why passengers fall backward when a bus starts suddenly.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: F = dp/dt (Force equals the rate of change of momentum). For constant mass, this simplifies to F = ma.
scientific_principles.application: Used to calculate the acceleration of a block being pulled or pushed on a surface, or the tension in strings of connected mass systems.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
scientific_principles.application: Explains the physics behind rocket propulsion, walking on the ground, and the recoil of a gun.

key_associations.extra_info: The heavier the object (greater mass), the greater its inertia, meaning it requires more force to change its state of motion.
The product of an object's mass and its velocity (p = mv). It is a conserved quantity in isolated systems.

sections.title: Friction and Dynamics
sections.description: The study of the resistive force that opposes relative motion or the tendency of such motion between two surfaces in contact.

key_concepts.explanation: The self-adjusting frictional force that acts when there is no relative sliding motion between surfaces. It maxes out at a value called 'limiting friction'.
The frictional force that comes into play when one body is actually sliding over the surface of another body. It is generally constant and slightly less than limiting static friction.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: f = μN (Frictional force is directly proportional to the normal reaction force).
scientific_principles.application: Crucial for calculating the acceleration of a body on a rough inclined plane or determining the maximum safe speed for a vehicle on a curved road.

important_facts.fact: The 'Angle of Repose' is the minimum angle of an inclined plane at which a body placed on it just begins to slide down due to its own weight.
